problem: Existing MultiON methods treat the task as a chain of single-object ObjectNav problems with a pre-given sequence of target classes (pre-sequenced MultiON, PSM), which is wasteful and impractical when the environment changes. Naive extensions of ObjectNav methods do not reward concurrent progress toward several target classes.
motivation: Humans searching for several objects do not fix an order; they progress toward several objects at once and adapt to unexpected sightings. An assistive robot should do the same, without computing a globally optimal (intractable) visiting order over all possible paths.
key_idea: Train an actor-critic long-term-goal policy on a semantic map with a reward that combines a sub-goal reward and a process reward for concurrently reducing geodesic distance to several target classes, so the robot picks up whichever object is convenient in any order.
insight: The reward design drives the gain: the process reward adds a bonus scaled by the fraction of remaining classes whose distance decreased, which pushes greedy, concurrent progress. SAM cuts timesteps and path length by about 50% versus PSM on paired episodes. It beats M-SemExp (whose reward is only the summed distance decrease) at every episode-length budget, and degrades more slowly as the step budget shrinks (e.g. 3-ON at 300 steps: 45.3 vs 32.49 success).
method: Semantic Mapping: Mask R-CNN semantic labels plus depth point clouds build a (C+2)×M×M allocentric semantic map (obstacles, explored area, C object classes), with random-shift augmentation, following SemExp.

Encoder Network: 4 conv layers (3×3, 32 channels), a FC layer with LayerNorm and tanh giving a 50-d embedding. Inputs are the semantic map, current and past positions, objects found so far, and a one-hot encoding of target classes (the new multi-class input).

Actor-Critic (DrQ-style): actor and critic have separate encoders, conv weights are updated only by the critic, clipped double Q-learning with 3-layer MLPs, and a replay buffer. A new long-term goal is sampled every 25 timesteps.
Deterministic Local Policy: Fast Marching Method on the obstacle channel gives the shortest path to the long-term goal, converted to move-forward 0.25 m, turn ±30°, and stop.

Reward = R_subgoal + 0.1·R_process − 0.01 per step: R_subgoal = 2 when an instance of any target class is reached. R_process is the total decrease in geodesic distance (from GT object locations in training) to the nearest instance of each remaining class, plus a bonus n/N when n of N classes got closer.
Sequence-agnostic training: about 1000 episodes of 2-ON or 3-ON on the 25 Gibson ObjectNav scenes, with random start positions.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN (pretrained) + conv encoder + actor-critic RL policy (trained from scratch) + Fast Marching Method local planner
setting.training_data: About 1000 k-ON episodes (k in {2,3}) on the 25 Gibson ObjectNav training scenes; Mask R-CNN is pretrained
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D (4×640×480) + pose + one-hot target class encoding
setting.action_space: Low-level: move-forward 0.25 m, turn-left/right 30°, stop (long-term goals every 25 steps with an analytical local planner)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth object locations used only for reward computation during training; noiseless pose given; none at test time otherwise

numbers.eval_set_note: Custom 2-ON test set: 5 held-out Gibson scenes x 200 episodes (1000 episodes total across 2-ON and 3-ON), not the official MultiON benchmark
numbers.extra: max 600 steps; success radius 1 m; trained on Gibson 25 scenes
numbers.evidence: Table II: SAM (ours) 70.7 / 72.3 success, 82.5 / 86.9 sub-success, 39.3 / 39.3 G-SPL for 2-ON / 3-ON

numbers.eval_set_note: Custom 3-ON test set: 5 held-out Gibson scenes x 200 episodes, not the official MultiON benchmark

numbers_note: The evaluation is on a custom Gibson-based 2-ON/3-ON set rather than the official MultiON benchmark (cylinder objects). Split naming is approximate: 5 unseen scenes. Table I gives timesteps and path length vs PSM per scene (e.g. Collierville 122 vs 242 steps, 16.16 vs 29.53 m).
results: SAM reaches 70.7% (2-ON) and 72.3% (3-ON) success with G-SPL 39.3, versus M-SemExp at 60.5/61.7 success and 30.5/29.8 G-SPL, and Random at 3.3/4.7. Against PSM on paired episodes, SAM roughly halves timesteps and path length (e.g. Darden 117 vs 248 steps).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation (Gibson/Habitat) with noiseless pose, on few scenes and only k≤3 (a small subset for 4-ON) because of limited object variety.
Not evaluated on the official MultiON benchmark, so results are not directly comparable with prior MultiON work; the PSM sequence is derived from the SAM run's order.
Greedy concurrent reward with no global planning; training needs GT object locations for the reward.
builds_on: Object goal navigation using data regularized Q-learning (DrQ-based ON)
